meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'делать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'делать'.

examples.text: Я вот думаю сделать его новым шеф-поваром.
examples.trans: I am thinking of making him the new head chef.

examples.text: Если будете вести себя хорошо, сделаете быструю карьеру.
examples.trans: If you behave well, you will make a fast career.

examples.text: Надеюсь, ты сделаешь всё быстро для моей дочери.
examples.trans: I hope you will do everything quickly for my daughter.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('new').

examples.text: Мы же хотели отпраздновать этот день вместе.
examples.trans: We wanted to celebrate this day together.

examples.text: Но я бы на твоём месте не волновался.
examples.trans: But if I were in your place I would not worry.

examples.text: А это директор Виктория и наш шеф-повар Виктор.

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'плохой'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('not bad, decent').

examples.text: Повар он неплохой, но в жизни полный беспорядок.

examples.trans: In my neighborhood there is a pretty good maternity hospital.

examples.text: Это на самом деле неплохой вариант.
examples.trans: This is actually not a bad option.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: In life we all look for a compromise one way or another.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'лный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('total').

examples.text: Повар он неплохой, но в жизни полный беспорядок.
examples.trans: He is not a bad cook, but his personal life is a complete mess.

examples.text: По работе у меня сегодня полный завал.
examples.trans: I am completely swamped at work today.

examples.text: Ладно, я полностью согласна на твои условия.
examples.trans: Fine, I completely agree to your terms.

meanings.note: Privative prefix 'бес-' ('without, -less', before voiceless consonants) (stem 'порядок'). Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'mess' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Повар он неплохой, но в жизни полный беспорядок.

examples.trans: To cause disturbances on the street.

examples.text: В комнате полный беспорядок.
examples.trans: There is complete disorder in the room.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'was'.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('married (of a man)').

examples.trans: So are you married now or not?

examples.text: Мой старший брат уже давно женат.
examples.trans: My older brother has been married for a long time.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'then, afterwards', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Правда, потом она себе их и забрала.
examples.trans: True, later she took them back for herself.

examples.trans: He was married to Vika, then he cheated on her.

examples.text: Я и так много времени на тебя потратила!
examples.trans: I have already spent too much time on you!

meanings.en: to cheat on, to be unfaithful to
meanings.note: Prefix 'из-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'менить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'changed', paired with 'изменять'.

examples.text: Он был женат на Вике, потом изменил ей.
examples.trans: He was married to Vika, then he cheated on her.

examples.text: Эдик, я хотела тебе изменить.
examples.trans: Edik, I wanted to cheat on you.

examples.text: Это ничего не изменит.
examples.trans: That won't change anything.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to her', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Правда, потом она себе их и забрала.
examples.trans: True, later she took them back for herself.

examples.text: Да, она внизу, ей что-нибудь нужно передать?
examples.trans: Yes, she is downstairs, should I pass anything on to her?

examples.text: Но в современном центре персонал гораздо получше.
examples.trans: But at a modern center the staff is much better.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'now', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: И как мне теперь работать? Душ сломался!

examples.text: А теперь у них скоро родится ребёнок.
examples.trans: And now they are going to have a baby soon.

examples.text: Теперь у меня из-за тебя будут серьёзные проблемы.
examples.trans: Now I am going to have serious problems because of you.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'at, near, with', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
